rationale:
There's no Lane C long-form today. The retatrutide TRANSCEND-T2D-2 result is about 55 hours old, has no tirzepatide arm, and we already covered it on 10-29 with both a long-form and the dysesthesia Short. The one-trial-per-week Short rule also rules out the retatrutide side-effect Short. So the long-form defaults to Lane A, using the last open item in the queue: hair loss. Bones and muscle, protein, stopping and plateau have all been done. Hair loss is a strong pick: the hair Short reached 142 on Instagram and 81 on YouTube on day 1, the Med Sci skin review from Oct 9 gives a fresh hook, and SURMOUNT-1 plus the label and the dermatology literature on telogen effluvium give settled evidence for 8–12 minutes. The last GLP-1 hair long-form (09-28) was semaglutide-led and 32 days ago, so it's outside the 30-day window. To keep it different from the 10-28 'how common' Short, the long-form centres on regrowth.

Shorts:
- 08:00: a calm 'honest uncertainty' Short on the rising tirzepatide-and-menopause story. It speaks to our large audience of women 45 and over, competition is low, and the twist is honest: the extra benefit linked to hormone therapy mostly showed up with semaglutide, not tirzepatide.
- 13:00: a tirzepatide-first head-to-head on a trial we haven't used (SURPASS-3 against insulin degludec). Head-to-head Shorts have a median of 106 views.
- 20:00: the funnel Short and the spin-off of L1. It's a myth-correction asking whether tirzepatide hair loss is permanent. The rotation only names a Lane C video when there is one, and on a non-Lane C day the house rule requires a spin-off of today's long-form, so it points to L1.

Carousel: carousels are still on until the owner removes them, so I followed the playbook and reused the verified text of the 10-26 tirzepatide blood pressure Short, with no new research. Blood pressure is proven on Instagram at 172.

Excluded: the compounded tirzepatide recall (already covered 10-21), the Reddit retatrutide story (covered 10-16), gallbladder and pancreas (covered 10-26 and 10-29), and Thanksgiving (that slot is Nov 10–18).

Variety: the pieces cover hair, hormones, blood sugar and blood pressure, and no pillar is used more than twice. Trend mix: about 40% rising or new hooks, 40% evergreen with a fresh hook, and 20% myth-busting.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide and hair loss: how common shedding was in the trials, why it happens (telogen effluvium after fast weight loss), when it usually starts and grows back, what helps, and when to see a clinician or dermatologist
pieces.angle: Same structure. Replace chapter (3) 'Med Sci (Basel) Oct 9, 2026 review' with: 'What do the 2026 reviews add?'. Use Gupta et al., Science Progress 2026 (PMC13100445): tirzepatide 5.4% vs placebo 0.9% in pooled trials, TE as the main pattern, typically reversible with improvement generally within 3–6 months after weight stabilises. Optionally add the Acta Diabetologica Oct 2026 review on trial vs real-world rates. Any observational relative risk gets 'linked to' plus absolute context, and the BMJ cohort is scoped to type 2 diabetes. Use the Med Sci (Basel) paper only if the scriptwriter can confirm it exists, with a working PubMed/MDPI URL, and quote it exactly.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Hair Loss: Does It Grow Back?
pieces.why:
Last open item in the Lane A queue (median about 158 watch minutes). Hair has proven demand (Instagram 142, YouTube 81 on day 1), the Oct 9 review gives a fresh hook, and it builds the suggested-video cluster with Protein and Strength. | fact-check: The topic is safe, useful and in-lane: Lane A, regrowth angle, red flags and the 'don't stop' line are all good. One problem: I couldn't confirm the 'Med Sci (Basel) systematic review, Oct 9, 2026'. Two targeted searches didn't find it. Don't build a chapter on a source that can't be confirmed. Verified alternatives:
(a) Gupta AK et al., 'GLP-1 therapies and hair loss: a systematic review…', Science Progress, Apr 17, 2026 (PMC13100445). It reports tirzepatide 5.4% vs placebo 0.9% (pooled trial data). It says TE is 'typically reversible with improvements generally observed within 3-6 months following stabilization of weight', with shedding 1.5–3 months after starting or a dose increase. That last point is a timing statement only: no dosing talk.
(b) Acta Diabetologica review, Oct 14, 2026 (Springer, s00592-026-02812-3). It notes that hair loss rates differ between trials and real-world settings.
(c) BMJ cohort (bmjgroup press release). Scope it to type 2 diabetes, say 'linked to', and give the absolute risk.
SURMOUNT-1 alopecia rates per arm vs placebo must be copied from the NEJM supplement or the Zepbound label. Mention the sex difference only if that source states it. Regrowth timing: say 'often within about 3–6 months after weight stabilises', as an average, not a promise. Kidney caveat on protein. Iron/thyroid/vitamin D only as 'ask your doctor about checking'. No supplement promises. Title is fine: 41 chars, drug first, and the first sentence answers it.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide and menopause hormone therapy: a Mayo Clinic real-world cohort of 2,379 women aged 45+ with BMI 27+ (The Menopause Society meeting; Healio, Oct 23, 2026)
pieces.angle: Keep the calm honest-uncertainty frame. Use this fact line: 'In a Mayo Clinic study of 2,379 women aged 45 and up, hormone therapy was linked to a bit more weight loss at one year: 11 percent versus 9.5 percent. That gap showed up with semaglutide. With tirzepatide, results leaned the same way early on but weren't statistically significant.' On screen: 'Observational · retrospective · conference data, not yet peer-reviewed · linked to, not proof'. Add: 'Researchers say hormone therapy isn't a weight-loss treatment. It's a separate choice to make with your clinician.' Keep the strength training, protein with kidney caveat, GI line, 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own', 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Loop ending, no emoji.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide in Menopause: Does HRT Add More? #shorts
pieces.why: Rising story with low creator competition. Women 45+ are a core audience, and the honest twist that the headline benefit is mostly semaglutide fits our calm format, which wins on Instagram and YouTube. | fact-check: Verified on Healio, Oct 23, 2026. Retrospective observational cohort, Mayo Clinic, presented by Regina Castaneda, MD at The Menopause Society meeting. 2,379 women aged 45+ with BMI ≥27 on semaglutide or tirzepatide. At 1 year: 11% vs 9.5% (P=.001). Healio says the significant differences were with semaglutide. For tirzepatide it reports only a 'similar directional effect' at early timepoints that 'did not reach statistical significance'. The angle's 'modest at 3 months and not significant after that' implies a significant 3-month result, and the source doesn't support that. Fix it. Other outlets (HealthDay/US News) give a different total (~3,900 women), so cite Healio's 2,379 only and don't mix in other figures. Note: an earlier, separate Mayo analysis (2025, 120 women on tirzepatide, 19.2% vs 14.0%) is what drove the 'hormone therapy boosts tirzepatide' headlines. If it's mentioned, label it as a separate, smaller observational study. Must say: hormone therapy isn't a weight-loss treatment (the researchers stressed this), and it's a separate decision with a clinician. Never suggest starting or stopping it. Title: drop 'HRT' (abbreviation) or keep it as the only abbreviation. Consider 'Tirzepatide in Menopause: Does Hormone Therapy Add More?'

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide vs insulin degludec in type 2 diabetes: the SURPASS-3 randomized head-to-head (Lancet 2021, adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, 52 weeks)
pieces.angle: Open: 'In adults with type 2 diabetes already on metformin, tirzepatide lowered A1C more than a long-acting insulin over a year. Weight went down on tirzepatide and up a little on insulin.' Give the A1C (% and mmol/mol) and weight change as a dose range for tirzepatide vs degludec, measured 'if everyone stayed on treatment', with per-arm n on screen. Add GI rates and low blood sugar rates exactly as the Lancet paper reports them. Honesty line: 'One open-label, company-funded trial, type 2 diabetes only. Insulin is still essential for many people.' Close: 'Bigger average isn't best for everyone. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.' Optional save/share line. No 'follow for more'. 170 words or fewer.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide vs Insulin for Type 2 Diabetes #shorts
pieces.why:
Tirzepatide-first head-to-heads have a median of 106 (signal, n=5). This one uses a new trial, so it follows the variety rule, and it brings in type 2 diabetes searchers. | fact-check: SURPASS-3 (Ludvik et al., Lancet 2021) is a real randomized, open-label, Lilly-funded 52-week trial of tirzepatide 5/10/15 mg vs titrated insulin degludec in adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin ± SGLT2 inhibitor. It's a legitimate new head-to-head for the lead slot. Fixes:
(1) The angle asks for 'the estimand'. Never say or show that word. Use 'if everyone stayed on treatment' (efficacy estimand) consistently for both arms.
(2) Three tirzepatide doses × A1C % × mmol/mol × weight × n won't fit in 170 words or on readable stat pills. Use the dose range ('across the three doses') with per-arm n on screen. Doses appear only as trial arm labels, never as guidance.
(3) Cut 'Follow for more.' Engagement lines ask to save or share only.
(4) Hypoglycaemia: quote the paper's threshold (<54 mg/dL or severe) and the per-arm rates exactly. Note it was lower on tirzepatide but present in both arms.
(5) GI rates per arm from the paper, briefly.
Keep 'insulin remains essential for many people', 'type 2 diabetes only', 'open-label, company-funded', and 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'. Never imply that someone on insulin should ask to swap. Frame it as a question for the prescriber about the overall treatment plan.

pieces.topic: Is tirzepatide hair loss permanent? Why telogen effluvium-type shedding usually grows back, and the signs that mean it's worth a doctor visit
pieces.angle: 20:00 funnel Short (Exp D) and spin-off of L1. It asks one fresh question rather than re-cutting L1 or repeating the 10-28 'how common' Short. Myth line: 'Hair loss on tirzepatide isn't usually permanent.' Answer within 10 s: shedding linked to fast weight loss (telogen effluvium) typically shows up a couple of months after the trigger and usually regrows over the following months. Use dermatology wording and averages, not predictions. Facts must match L1's verified script exactly. Red flags for a dermatologist: lasts more than about 6 months, comes in patches, scarring or painful. What helps: enough protein (kidney caveat), and ask your doctor about iron, thyroid and vitamin D checks. No supplements. One GI line. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice' plus the prescriber line. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.' No spoken titles. 170 words or fewer. Mix at 0.02 or lower.

pieces.topic: Your first Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: how a smaller appetite and slower stomach emptying can change a big holiday meal, and practical, guilt-free ways to plan the plate, pace, drinks and leftovers so the day feels good
pieces.angle: Lane A (log 'lane: A'), 'Life on Tirzepatide' series, 8–12 min, 14:00 ET, evergreen, no news peg. The first spoken sentence answers the title with a 'you' scenario: 'Your first Thanksgiving on tirzepatide can feel different: you may fill up faster, and big, rich meals may sit heavier. A little planning, mostly around protein, portion size and pace, helps you enjoy it.' Chapters named as searched questions: (1) Why does a big meal feel different on tirzepatide? Credit only the FDA label wording (it can delay gastric emptying; GI side effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common). (2) What should I put on my plate? Build it around turkey or another protein you enjoy, then whatever else you like. Credit only what the 2025 ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS advisory (Mozaffarian et al., Obesity 2025, PMC12304835) says: getting enough protein, and that 'avoiding fatty or high fiber foods during the first few days of treatment' can ease nausea. Quote that exact scope and don't stretch it to holidays. Smaller plates, starting with a small serving and going back if you're still hungry, and leftovers boxes are our own tips with no source tag. (3) How fast should I eat? Eating slowly and stopping when comfortably full are our own tips, untagged. (4) What about drinks? Sip fluids through the day unless you've been told to limit fluids. The label warns that vomiting or diarrhoea can cause dehydration. For alcohol, make no sourced claim: ask your prescriber. If you also take insulin or a sulfonylurea, the label notes a higher risk of low blood sugar, so ask your prescriber about the holiday. (5) What if I feel too full or queasy? Common comfort steps, plus the label's warning signs (severe stomach pain that won't go away) and 'contact your healthcare provider'. (6) Leftovers, the next day and movement: an optional walk after the meal is our own tip; the advisory's strength-training point stays at its exact wording. (7) Mindset: no guilt, no foods labelled 'bad', no calorie talk, no 'earning' food, and enjoying the people as much as the plate. Anyone with a history of disordered eating should follow their care team's plan. Explicitly say: don't skip, move or change your injection or dose around the holiday on your own; that's a conversation with your prescriber. Never mention dose numbers. Re-hook every 45–75 s. One subscribe ask, after the plate payoff. Include 'Not personal advice', 'don't stop or change your medicines on your own' and the full prescriber line. Ending: 'There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description.' No spoken titles and never 'on screen'. Thumbnail: 4 words or fewer, a warm reaction layout with one labelled character at a holiday table (e.g. 'Full Already?'). Sources: the joint advisory and the FDA Zepbound/Mounjaro label only. Drop the YouGov hook unless a primary URL can be opened.
